name: KOVAL Distillery tours and tastings (Ravenswood)

Cocktail classes: make 3-4 drinks with a bartender (dates vary)

name: Vito's Vault (Roaring '20s speakeasy dinner show)
hook: 1920s speakeasy dinner show with a live musical revue
description: A small speakeasy-style dinner theater in Jefferson Park where Vito and his cast put on an audience-interactive musical comedy revue after a three-course dinner and dessert. From late November it switches to an Old Fashioned Christmas Spectacular, and New Year's Eve adds a costume contest, champagne toast and dancing. Tell them you're celebrating and Vito announces it from the stage.

good_to_know: Doors at 6pm, show 7:30pm (NYE doors 7pm). Holiday cocktails extra. Weekday matinees on request.

hours_note: Doors 6pm, show 7:30pm. New Year's Eve doors 7pm with a midnight toast and dancing.

price_note: $49.50-$91 a ticket plus booking fee, by seating zone.
hook: Love songs by candlelight under a stained-glass dome

name: Blue Man Group: A New Holiday Surprise (CIBC Theatre)
description: Blue Man Group's all-new holiday show: holiday songs on their homemade instruments, drumming, comedy and audience participation, in a Loop Broadway theater.
address: CIBC Theatre, 18 W Monroe St, Chicago, IL 60603
hook: Blue Man Group's brand-new holiday show

name: Richardson Christmas Tree Farm (cut your own tree)
hook: Hunt down and cut your own Christmas tree on a 75-acre farm
description: A big choose-and-cut Christmas tree farm near the Wisconsin line, with more than 50,000 trees of many kinds spread over 75 acres. Walk the rows to pick your tree, then warm up in the heated barn with fresh donuts and browse hundreds of wreaths and decorations.
highlights: Cut your own or pick a pre-cut tree
Staff shake, net and can haul your tree
Free wagon ride to the fields on weekends
Heated sales barn with restrooms and fresh donuts
address: 9407 Richardson Rd, Spring Grove, IL 60081
price_note: Free entry. Current posted tree prices (no year given, so they may change): cut-your-own $98 plus tax, any size; select field trees from $69; pre-cut trees $98-$350 plus tax. Cash, check or card.

season.note: Open the day after Thanksgiving through December 20.

hours_note: The tree fields have no lights, so come before sunset to pick a tree; the pre-cut trees are in a lit area.

name: Glow Putt Mini Golf & Arcade (Waikiki)
hook: Glow-in-the-dark mini golf inside the Hyatt
description: Hawaii's original glow-in-the-dark mini golf, with a newer Waikiki course and arcade tucked inside the Hyatt Regency. An easy, goofy indoor date when it rains or after dinner on Kalakaua.
highlights: Open daily 10am-9pm, last play 1 hour before close
address: Hyatt Regency Waikiki, 2424 Kalakaua Ave, Honolulu, HI 96815
price_note: $20 ages 6+; $18 kama'aina, military, first responders and seniors with ID; $10 ages 5 and under; same-day replay $10 ($5 keiki).
hours_note: Last play starts 1 hour before closing.

name: The Escape Game Honolulu
hook: 60-minute escape rooms in Ala Moana Center
description: Live escape rooms at Ala Moana Center where your group has an hour to crack clues and get out, with themes like a heist, a gold rush, a submarine and a prison break. The old Breakout Waikiki site now sends visitors here.
highlights: Book online; other players may join if spots are open
address: Ala Moana Center, 1450 Ala Moana Blvd, Suite 2404, Honolulu, HI 96814
hours_note: Games run at booked times only.

name: Blade & Timber Axe Throwing Honolulu
hook: Axe throwing with a bar in Kakaʻako
description: Coached axe-throwing lanes in Kakaʻako, with the Whetstone Bar serving food, beer and cocktails between throws. A loud, competitive night out that works for a date or a group.
highlights: Lanes for groups of 1-18; 19+ ask about private events
Sign the waiver online before you go
address: 506 Keawe St, Honolulu, HI 96813
hours_note: Hours may change on holidays and for private events.

photos.credit: Blade & Timber Axe Throwing Honolulu (official site)

name: Lucky Strike Honolulu
hook: Boutique bowling and arcade at Ala Moana
description: A small, lounge-style bowling alley inside Ala Moana Center with an arcade, darts and a sports bar. Good for a rainy afternoon or a late game after shopping.
highlights: 4 bowling lanes plus arcade and darts
Night Strike: unlimited bowling with shoes $30.99 (Sun from 6pm, Mon-Thu from 7pm)
Half-price bowling and arcade Tue and Wed
Lanes bookable up to 8 days ahead
address: Ala Moana Center, 1450 Ala Moana Blvd, Honolulu, HI 96814
price_note: $11.99-$16.99 per game per person depending on day and time; shoes $6.99.
hours_note: Hours change week to week; check before you go.

name: ʻOhana Entertainment Center at Waikiki Beach Marriott
hook: New Waikiki game room: 60+ arcade games, bowling, VR
description: A new 6,000 sq ft game room off the Waikiki Beach Marriott lobby with more than 60 arcade games, boutique bowling, virtual reality and sports simulators. It is open to everyone, not just hotel guests.
highlights: 60+ arcade games, boutique bowling, VR, sports simulators
Open to visitors and locals, not only hotel guests
address: Waikiki Beach Marriott Resort & Spa (lobby), 2552 Kalakaua Ave, Honolulu, HI 96815
hours_note: Hours not posted; check with the hotel before you go.

name: Great Big Game Show Honolulu
hook: Star in your own TV-style game show
description: A real studio with a live host where your group competes in rounds of physical and puzzle mini-games like Blaster Blitz and Build It Up. Feels like being on a TV game show, which makes it a fun pick for friends or a playful date.
highlights: Book a show online; sign the waiver at check-in
Groups of 15+ book as an event
address: Ala Moana Center, 1450 Ala Moana Blvd, Space #2404, Honolulu, HI 96814
hours_note: Shows run at booked times only.

name: Aya Golf Lounge
hook: Golf simulators and karaoke rooms near Ala Moana
description: An upscale indoor golf lounge with Golfzon simulators in private rooms, drinks, small bites and karaoke. A relaxed way to play a famous course without leaving town.
highlights: Drinks, small bites and karaoke nights
Parking on the Azure Ala Moana retail level
address: Azure Ala Moana, 641 Keeaumoku St, Suite 1, Honolulu, HI 96814
hours_note: Hours not posted online; call before you go.

name: Free Hawaiian Culture Classes at Royal Hawaiian Center
hook: Free lei, ukulele, hula and weaving lessons
description: Royal Hawaiian Center hosts free hour-long lessons on weekdays: 'ukulele on Mondays, hula on Tuesdays, lauhala weaving on Wednesdays and orchid lei making on Fridays. A sweet, low-key way to learn something Hawaiian in the middle of Waikiki.
highlights: Free, first come first served, ages 10+ for 'ukulele and lei
address: Royal Hawaiian Center, 2201 Kalakaua Ave, Honolulu, HI 96815
price_note: Free.
hours_note: Mon 'ukulele (Helumoa Hale, Building B, Level 1); Tue hula (The Royal Grove); Wed lauhala weaving and Fri lei making (Building C, Level 2). No reservations; spots go to the first guests.

name: KraftStories Craft Workshops (Chinatown)
hook: Make a rug, mosaic lamp or terrarium in Chinatown
description: A Chinatown craft studio running small hands-on workshops: rug tufting, Turkish mosaic lamps, sea glass art, terrariums and wooden lei, plus a Turkish coffee tasting brewed on hot sand. You leave with something you made, which makes it a good date or rainy-day plan.
highlights: Rug tufting 2.5 h ($119), mosaic lamp 2 h ($99)
Sea glass art 1 h ($59), terrarium 1.5 h ($49)
Workshops run several times a week; book online
address: 15 N Pauahi St, Honolulu, HI 96817
price_note: $49-$119 each, depending on the workshop; kama'aina discount for locals.
hours_note: Booking-only workshops; pick a date and time when you book.

name: Waikiki Aquarium
hook: Hawaiian reef life on the edge of Kapiʻolani Park
description: A small oceanfront aquarium at the Diamond Head end of Waikiki, focused on Hawaiian and Pacific marine life. An easy hour that pairs well with a walk through Kapiʻolani Park.
address: 2777 Kalakaua Ave, Honolulu, HI 96815
price_note: $12 general; $8 kama'aina, military and Hawai'i students; $5 ages 4-12, seniors 65+ and visitors with disabilities; 3 and under free.
hours_note: Building closes at 5 pm. Thanksgiving 9 am-2:30 pm; New Year's Day 11 am-4:30 pm. Closed Dec 13 (Honolulu Marathon) and Dec 25. Open during renovations.
age_note: Under 18 must be with an adult.

name: Honolulu Zoo
hook: A tropical zoo steps from Waikiki Beach
description: A leafy zoo at the edge of Kapiʻolani Park, a short walk from the Waikiki hotels, with an African savanna, primates and reptiles. Easy to combine with the aquarium and a park picnic.
address: 151 Kapahulu Ave, Honolulu, HI 96815
price_note: $21 adults 13+, $13 kids 3-12, under 3 free; kama'aina (Hawai'i ID) and military $10 adults, $6 kids.

name: Honolulu Zoo Twilight Tour
hook: Walk the zoo after the gates close
description: A two-hour guided evening walk through parts of the Honolulu Zoo after closing, visiting areas like the African Savanna, Primate Island and the reptiles. A calmer, more unusual way to see the zoo, and a nice early-evening date.
highlights: Runs rain or shine; meet at Gate #6
address: Honolulu Zoo, Gate #6, 151 Kapahulu Ave, Honolulu, HI 96815
price_note: $30 adults, $25 kids 2-12; kama'aina $25/$20; zoo members $20/$15; under 2 free.
hours_note: Booking only; dates and start times are shown when you book. Arrive 15 minutes early at Gate #6.

photos.credit: Robert Linsdell from St. Andrews, Canada / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0)

name: Foster Botanical Garden
hook: Giant 1850s trees in a 14-acre Chinatown garden
description: A 14-acre city garden on the edge of Chinatown with towering 'exceptional trees' (some planted in the 1850s), a palm garden, a prehistoric cycad glen, an outdoor butterfly garden and a conservatory. A shady, quiet stroll that costs almost nothing.
address: 180 N Vineyard Blvd, Honolulu, HI 96817
price_note: $5 adults, $3 Hawai'i residents, $1 kids 6-12, under 5 free; annual family pass $25.
hours_note: Last garden admission is 3:30 pm; all guests must exit by 4:00 pm. Closed Dec 25 and Jan 1.

photos.credit: City and County of Honolulu, Dept. of Parks and Recreation (official site)

name: SKY Waikiki
hook: 19th-floor rooftop with sunset views over Waikiki
description: A rooftop bar and restaurant on the 19th floor above Kalakaua Avenue with wide views over Waikiki and the sunset. Come for a sunset drink, or late on Friday and Saturday when it turns into a nightlife spot.
highlights: Dinner: no wet beachwear; nightlife: closed-toe shoes
address: 2270 Kalakaua Ave, 19th Floor, Honolulu, HI 96815
price_note: Happy hour 4-6 pm: $4 oysters, $5 Modelo, $10 bubbly.
hours_note: Nightlife Fri-Sat from 9 pm. Dress code: no wet beachwear at dinner; closed-toe shoes and no beachwear, slippers or tank tops for nightlife.

name: Friday Night Fireworks at Hilton Hawaiian Village
hook: Free fireworks over Waikiki Beach every Friday
address: Hilton Hawaiian Village beachfront, 2005 Kalia Rd, Honolulu, HI 96815
hours_note: Fridays at 7:45 pm. Times can change; check the resort calendar.
description: Every Friday evening the Hilton Hawaiian Village sets off a fireworks show just offshore, visible from the beach in front of the resort. Bring a towel to the sand after dinner for an easy, classic Waikiki date.
highlights: Watch from Waikiki Beach in front of the resort
price_note: Price not posted; the show is visible from the beach in front of the resort.

photos.credit: Daniel Ramirez from Honolulu, USA / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0)

name: 'Twas the Light Before Christmas on Ice
hook: Indoor holiday lights and an ice rink in Honolulu
description: A holiday light walk-through with an indoor ice rink inside the Hawaiʻi Convention Center. Skating in Hawaii in December is the novelty here, and it makes a festive evening date.
highlights: Skating is an add-on; skate rental included with skate tickets
Weekday skaters unlimited time, weekends 1.5 h
address: Hawaiʻi Convention Center, 1801 Kalakaua Ave, Honolulu, HI 96815
price_note: Prices vary by date and time; skating costs extra.

season.note: Holiday season only: Dec 1, 2026 to Jan 3, 2027.

hours_note: Dec 1-4 and 7-9: 3-10 pm. Dec 5: 3-10 pm. Dec 6 and Dec 10-31: 10 am-10 pm. Jan 1-3: 10 am-7 pm. Last tickets 9 pm in December.
age_note: Kids under 2 can't go on the ice.

name: Kakaʻako Farmers Market at Ward Village
hook: Saturday market of local farms and food stalls
description: A weekly Saturday market at Ward Village with fruit, vegetables and flowers from Hawaiʻi farms plus grab-and-go food stalls. A relaxed morning stop before walking the Kakaʻako murals nearby.
highlights: Pairs with the Kaka'ako mural walk
address: 919 Ala Moana Blvd, Honolulu, HI

name: Holokai Catamaran Sunset Sail (Waikiki)
hook: Open-bar sunset sail that boards right off Waikiki Beach
description: A sailing catamaran pushes off the sand in front of the Outrigger Reef and cruises the Waikiki coast at golden hour, with Diamond Head and the Honolulu skyline glowing behind you. The open bar pours beer, wine, bubbly and the house cocktail while you lounge on the nets.
highlights: Open bar: beer, wine, champagne, hard seltzer, house cocktail
Reef-safe sunscreen and motion-sickness aid on board
address: Check-in at Outrigger Reef Waikiki Beach Resort, 2169 Kalia Rd, Honolulu, HI 96815
age_note: All ages Saturday to Thursday; Friday sails 21+. Under 18 must be with an adult.
price_note: $80 each for adults 13+, $45 kids 4-12, under 4 free.
hours_note: Sails 5:00-6:30 pm October to February, 5:30-7:00 pm March to September. Check in 30 minutes before.

name: Holokai Catamaran Turtle Canyon Snorkel (Waikiki)
hook: Sail off Waikiki Beach and snorkel with green sea turtles
description: A sail-and-snorkel trip from the sand in Waikiki to Turtle Canyon, a reef about 30 feet deep where Hawaiian green sea turtles come to feed and get cleaned by fish. An in-water guide leads the swim, then you sail back along the Honolulu coastline.
highlights: 2.5 hours: about 75 min snorkeling, 75 min sailing
Gear, vest, in-water guide, snacks and soft drinks included
Drinks for sale on board ($5, cash only)
Wild turtles: sightings not guaranteed; give them space and don't touch
address: Check-in at Outrigger Reef Waikiki Beach Resort, 2169 Kalia Rd, Honolulu, HI 96815
age_note: All ages; under 18 must be with an adult and need a parent's waiver. You should be a comfortable swimmer.
price_note: $80 each (ages 4+).
hours_note: Two trips: 9:00-11:30 am (check in 8:30) and 12:00-2:30 pm (check in 11:30). Groups of 16+ book by phone or email.

photos.credit: Holokai Catamaran Turtle Canyon Snorkel (Waikiki) (official site)

name: Holokai Catamaran Whale Watch Sail (Waikiki)
hook: Look for humpbacks off Waikiki, drink in hand
description: In humpback season this beach-launched catamaran heads out off Waikiki to look for whales that migrate to Hawaii for the winter. It is a short afternoon sail with an open bar, so it fits easily into a beach day.
address: Check-in at Outrigger Reef Waikiki Beach Resort, 2169 Kalia Rd, Honolulu, HI 96815
price_note: From $50.
hours_note: Sails 3:00-4:30 pm.

season.note: Whale season sailing, December 1 to March 31.

photos.credit: Holokai Catamaran Whale Watch Sail (Waikiki) (official site)

name: Hawaii Nautical Dolphin Watch and Turtle Snorkel Sail (Ko Olina)
hook: Watch spinner dolphins, then snorkel with turtles, lunch and bar included
description: A 3-hour sail along the West Oahu coast to watch wild spinner dolphins from the boat, then a guided snorkel with green sea turtles and reef fish. The operator is NOAA Dolphin SMART recognized and does not offer swim-with-dolphins trips.
highlights: Dolphin sighting guarantee: re-ride if none are seen
Packed lunch and full bar included
65-foot catamaran with restrooms and freshwater shower
Free outer-lot parking; free shuttle from Ko Olina resorts
address: Ko Olina Marina Building, 92-100 Waipahe Pl, Kapolei, HI 96707
age_note: All ages; no snorkel experience needed.
price_note: Adults from $149.95, children from $99.95. Paid marina parking $22 if the outer lot is full.
hours_note: Daily 9:00 am to 12:00 pm. Arrive by 8:40 am; boarding closes 10 minutes before departure.

photos.credit: Hawaii Nautical Dolphin Watch and Turtle Snorkel Sail (Ko Olina) (official site)

name: Ko Olina Ocean Adventures Snorkel and Sail
hook: One uncrowded catamaran: snorkel, hot lunch and dolphins from a distance
description: A family-run company with a single 53-foot sailing catamaran out of Ko Olina Marina, offering a 3-hour snorkel sail (morning for calmer water, afternoon for brighter reef light) and a 2-hour sunset sail with pupus. Spinner dolphins live along this coast year round; the captain keeps the legal 50-yard distance and you watch from the boat.
highlights: Snorkel sail: 3 hours, 45-minute guided snorkel, hot buffet lunch
Three drinks included for 21+ (with ID), unlimited soft drinks
Sunset sail: 2 hours with Hawaiian appetizers and three drinks
Humpback whales in winter, dolphins all year
Barefoot boat; marina parking $20 a day
address: Marina Activities desk, Ko Olina Marina, 92-100 Waipahe Pl, Kapolei, HI 96707
age_note: Drinks for 21+ with valid ID. Mornings recommended for small children and first-time snorkelers.
price_note: Ages 13+: snorkel sail $195 ($225 with round-trip Waikiki transport); sunset sail $130. Children 4-12 and infants pay less.
hours_note: Snorkel sails 8:30-11:30 am (check in 8:00) and 1:00-4:00 pm. Sunset sail 4:30-6:30 pm (check in 4:15) January-March and September-December; 5:00-7:00 pm April-August.

photos.credit: Ko Olina Ocean Adventures Snorkel and Sail (official site)

name: Magnum Helicopters Doors-Off Tour
hook: Fly over Oahu with the doors off
description: A 50-minute doors-off helicopter flight from Honolulu over the skyline, Pearl Harbor, mountain waterfalls and the coast, in the same aircraft used for TV shoots. Nothing between you and the view, and the pilot narrates as you go.
highlights: Doors off; front seats can be reserved (weight rules apply)
Check in 45 minutes early; no hotel shuttle
Phones allowed only on a strap
address: 130 Iolana Pl, Honolulu, HI 96819
age_note: Ages 10 and up; weight limits apply.
hours_note: Flights by reservation. Office phone line daily 8 am-6 pm. Free cancellation up to 48 hours before; weather cancellations are rescheduled or refunded.

name: Blue Hawaiian Helicopters: Complete Island Oahu
hook: See the whole island from the air in about an hour
description: A narrated 65-minute helicopter loop from Honolulu that takes in Pearl Harbor and the Arizona Memorial, hidden rainforest valleys and waterfalls, the North Shore surf breaks and the windward coast. Blue Hawaiian also flies North Shore tours from the Ritz-Carlton Turtle Bay.
highlights: Pearl Harbor, Windward valleys, North Shore beaches
Second heliport at Turtle Bay on the North Shore
address: Honolulu Heliport, 99 Kaulele Pl, Honolulu, HI 96819
hours_note: Flights by reservation.

photos.credit: Blue Hawaiian Helicopters: Complete Island Oahu (official site)

name: Outrigger Canoe Surfing with Waikiki Beach Services
hook: Paddle a Hawaiian outrigger canoe and ride a Waikiki wave
description: Climb into a traditional outrigger canoe with Waikiki Beachboys, paddle out together and catch a wave back toward the beach, a Waikiki tradition that is hard to do anywhere else. The same beach stand at the Royal Hawaiian and Sheraton also runs surf and stand-up paddle lessons.
highlights: Check in right on the sand; no shop walk
Operating since 1955 with licensed Waikiki Beachboys
address: On the beach at the Royal Hawaiian, 2259 Kalakaua Ave, Honolulu, HI 96815 (also at the Sheraton Waikiki, 2255 Kalakaua Ave)
price_note: Canoe surfing from $48 each; surf lessons from $95 each.

only_here.reason: Riding Waikiki's waves in an outrigger canoe, steered by a beach boy

photos.credit: Outrigger Canoe Surfing with Waikiki Beach Services (official site)

name: Hans Hedemann Surf School (Waikiki)
hook: Learn to surf in Waikiki from a pro surfer's family school
description: A family-owned surf school founded by former pro surfer Hans Hedemann, running group, semi-private and private beginner lessons in the gentle waves off Waikiki. Board and rash guard are provided, and the school promises you will ride waves during the lesson.
highlights: Group lessons for ages 14+; private lessons suit kids and first-timers
Surf top included; sunscreen for sale
Meets at the shop in the Queen Kapiolani Hotel, next to the Honolulu Zoo
Also has a North Shore location
address: Queen Kapiolani Hotel, 150 Kapahulu Ave, Honolulu, HI 96815
price_note: Each: group $100, semi-private $150, private $180.
hours_note: Shop hours; lessons by booking.

name: Kailua Beach Adventures: Mokulua Islands Kayak Tour
hook: Paddle 2.5 miles to the Mokes and land on a seabird island
description: A guided 5-hour kayak trip from Kailua across turtle feeding grounds to the Mokulua (Twin) Islands, a seabird sanctuary where landing needs a permit. The tour includes the permit, a guided walk among nesting seabirds, beach time and snorkeling; it is a workout, aimed at athletic or experienced paddlers.
highlights: Island landing permits included; none issued on Sundays
About 60-80 min paddle each way, 45-min island eco walk
Group tours ages 13+; private tours from age 8
Free Waikiki shuttle for the 9 am tour
You wheel the kayak to the beach yourself (required by law)
address: 130 Kailua Rd, Suite 101B, Kailua, HI 96734
age_note: Group tours 13+ (ages 13-16 in a double kayak with a parent); private tours 8+. Under 18 with a parent or guardian.
price_note: Group tour $249 (13+). Private $439 per person for 1-2 people, $339 per person for 3+. Easier Popoia (Flat) Island tour from $179. Kayak rentals from $74.
hours_note: Monday to Saturday. 9 am tour has a Waikiki shuttle (back about 4 pm). Free reschedule more than 48 hours ahead.

photos.credit: Kailua Beach Adventures: Mokulua Islands Kayak Tour (official site)

name: North Shore Shark Adventures (cage snorkel)
hook: Float in a cage 3 miles out while sharks circle
description: A boat from Haleiwa Harbor runs 3 miles offshore, where you climb into a floating cage at the surface and watch sharks swim around you in open water; dolphins and turtles sometimes show up on the way. No scuba or swimming skill is needed, and the company has run these trips since 2001.
highlights: No swimming required; cage floats at the surface
All ages (with conditions on the site)
address: Haleiwa Boat Harbor, 66-105 Haleiwa Rd, Haleiwa, HI 96712
age_note: All ages (the site adds conditions; see booking page).
price_note: From $90 each.
hours_note: Trips by reservation.

photos.credit: North Shore Shark Adventures (cage snorkel) (official site)

name: Skydive Hawaii (tandem jump over the North Shore)
hook: Tandem skydive from 14,000 feet over the North Shore
description: Hawaii's longest-running skydiving company, family owned since 1984, flies tandem jumpers up from historic Kawaihapai (Dillingham) Airfield and drops them over the North Shore coastline with a licensed USPA instructor. A 20,000-foot HALO jump with oxygen is offered for the extra-brave.
highlights: Tandem from 14,000 ft; HALO from 20,000 ft (book 4 days ahead)
$20 fuel surcharge and 3.5% card fee on top
Walk-in slots limited; shuttle service on request
address: Kawaihapai (Dillingham) Airfield, 68-760 Farrington Hwy, Waialua, HI 96791
age_note: 18 and older; 250 lb weight limit (surcharge over 200 lb).
price_note: Each: 14,000 ft tandem $198 online special (deposit, limited slots) or $245 standard; 20,000 ft HALO from $2,000 ($1,600 each for 3+). $20 fuel surcharge per tandem. $20 off the standard jump with military or student ID.
hours_note: Plan to be on site 2-4 hours or more.

name: Hawaii Water Sports Center (parasail, tubes, wakeboard)
hook: Parasail, banana boat and bumper tubes in Hawaii Kai
description: A water-sports base on Koko Marina in Hawaii Kai where you can parasail above Maunalua Bay, bounce around on banana boats and bumper tubes, wakeboard or waterski, or take a boat out to snorkel with turtles. Combos bundle several rides into one loud, splashy morning.
highlights: Parasailing, banana boat, bumper tube, wakeboard, waterski
Near Hanauma Bay, east of Waikiki
address: Koko Marina Center, 7192 Kalanianaole Hwy, Honolulu, HI 96825
price_note: Parasailing $89; banana boat or bumper tube $59; wakeboard, waterski or turtle snorkel $129; combos $99-$219.

name: Kaneohe Bay Ocean Sports: Sandbar Tour
hook: Catamaran to the Kaneohe sandbar with live Hawaiian music
description: A 70-foot catamaran takes you into Kaneohe Bay to the sandbar (Ahu o Laka), where you stand in knee-deep water in the middle of the bay under the Ko'olau mountains. The trip mixes snorkeling, paddleboarding, sandbar volleyball and live Hawaiian music, with optional bumper tube and banana boat rides.
highlights: Snorkel, stand-up paddle, volleyball, live music
All-inclusive option adds bumper tube and banana boat
Runs Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri, Sat
address: He'eia Kea Small Boat Harbor, 46-499 Kamehameha Hwy, Kaneohe, HI 96744
price_note: Morning standard from $90, all-inclusive from $130; afternoon standard from $100, all-inclusive from $140.
hours_note: Departures 9:30 am and 1:00 pm, about 3.5 hours each. Closed Sundays, Wednesdays and federal holidays.

name: Bike Hawaii E-Bike Tour: Honolulu Rainforest Ride
hook: E-bike up into the rainforest high above Honolulu
description: A guided e-bike ride on a paved mountain road in the Ko'olau range above Honolulu, about 10 miles with 1,600 feet of climbing made easy by the motor. You ride through eucalyptus, bamboo and banyan forest, sometimes through the clouds, with city and ocean views and a naturalist guide.
highlights: E-bike, helmet and nature guide included
Riders 14+ and at least 5 ft tall; weight limit applies
Bring your own water and snacks
address: Meet at Archie Baker Park, Makiki, Honolulu
age_note: 14 and older, at least 5 ft tall; must know how to ride a bike; weight limit applies.
price_note: $140 each (adult or child). Private option costs more.
hours_note: Daily, 8:00-11:00 am; meet at 8:15 am at Archie Baker Park or choose a hotel pickup.

photos.credit: Bike Hawaii E-Bike Tour: Honolulu Rainforest Ride (official site)

name: Hawaii Eco Divers: Discover Scuba (no certification)
hook: Try scuba for the first time from an Oahu beach
description: A beginner Discover Scuba shore dive with no certification needed: a short lesson, then a guided dive among reef fish and turtles. In summer it runs at Shark's Cove in the Pupukea marine conservation district; when winter swells hit the North Shore it moves to Electric Beach on the west side.
highlights: No experience needed; ages 10+ in good health
Summer: Shark's Cove; winter: Electric Beach (West Oahu)
Also runs PADI courses and certified boat and wreck dives
address: Shark's Cove, Pupukea (summer); Electric Beach, West Oahu (winter). Shop based in Haleiwa, HI 96712
age_note: Ages 10 and up, in good physical condition.
price_note: $155 each plus tax; a second dive is $45.
hours_note: By reservation.

season.note: Shore site changes with the surf: Shark's Cove in summer, Electric Beach in winter.

photos.credit: Hawaii Eco Divers: Discover Scuba (no certification) (official site)

name: Hawaii Glass Bottom Boats (Waikiki cruise)
hook: Watch reefs and shipwrecks through the floor, BYOB
description: A one-hour power-catamaran cruise from Kewalo Basin toward Diamond Head, looking down through a glass floor at live reef and sometimes a shipwreck, with humpbacks possible from November to May. Bring your own drinks; Friday nights there is also a fireworks cruise off Waikiki.
highlights: Sunset cruise 1.5 hours; Friday fireworks cruise
address: Kewalo Basin Harbor, 1025 Ala Moana Blvd, Slip F21, Honolulu, HI
age_note: All ages; 21+ to drink alcohol on board.
price_note: Daytime cruise from $40; sunset cruise from $60; fireworks cruise from $60.
hours_note: Daily cruises; times show when you book. Fireworks cruise Fridays at 7:30 pm.

photos.credit: Hawaii Glass Bottom Boats (Waikiki cruise) (official site)

name: Atlantis Submarines Waikiki
hook: Dive 100 feet down off Waikiki in a real submarine
description: A real battery-powered passenger submarine, Atlantis XIV, takes you more than 100 feet below the surface off Waikiki, past artificial reefs and sunken ships where turtles, sharks and reef fish gather, all while you stay dry in air-conditioned comfort. It is the world's largest passenger submarine, carrying 64 people, with Diamond Head in view on the boat ride out.
highlights: Download the audio tour before you go (no Wi-Fi below)
address: Atlantis kiosk, Hilton Hawaiian Village beachfront (in front of the Ali'i Tower, next to Tropics Bar and Grill), 2005 Kalia Rd, Honolulu, HI 96815
hours_note: Dives by reservation.

name: Coral Crater Adventure Park: 2-Person ATV

Card only; no pets except service animals

Fridays and Saturdays bring hip-hop, Top 40 and dance DJs from 10pm to 4am.

It is about 20 minutes from Waikiki and an easy stop on the way to Kailua or Lanikai.

VIP: spears, shovels, ninja stars; cosmic glow option

Play Pass: 1 hr golf + 1 hr axe throwing + $20 arcade tokens
50% off sims when you bring your own clubs Wed, Thu, Sun

hours_note: Thanksgiving and Christmas hours not posted.

name: K1 Speed Las Vegas
hook: Indoor electric go-kart racing a few minutes west of the Strip
description: Indoor electric kart track where you race short heats against friends and strangers and get your lap times on a scoreboard afterward. Quick heats, no gas fumes and climate-controlled, with a paddock lounge to hang out between races.

Groups of 8+ can book private events

1-on-1 coach, racing suit and helmet, full insurance
Packages by lap count (5 to 15 laps)

price_note: Ride-along from $99; supercar from $199; GT race car from $399.

hours_note: Thanksgiving and Christmas hours not posted.

name: Battlefield Vegas
hook: Military-themed gun range with free Humvee pickup from the Strip

A la carte from $25, packages from $125

Free pickup with indoor packages over $200

El Loco: steep drops and sharp turns
hours_note: Thanksgiving and Christmas hours not posted.

Other Vegas locations: Planet Hollywood's Miracle Mile Shops and Town Square

Late-night menu midnight to 1 am in the bar

Parking on site; no restrooms or public transport

description: On December weekends the Nevada State Railroad Museum in Boulder City turns its heritage train ride into a Santa Train. You board a vintage railroad car for a ride out toward Henderson and back while holiday songs play and everyone sings along. Santa and his helpers walk through the cars handing out candy canes and stopping for photos. Seats are limited and the museum says to book early; it is aimed at families but works as a sweet, low-key outing with friends, and the museum's open-air train pavilion is next door.

description: Enchant fills the Las Vegas Ballpark in Summerlin with what it bills as the world's largest Christmas light maze, this year a storyline called The Great Search where you hunt for Santa's missing reindeer among glowing light sculptures. General admission also covers the shopping village with seasonal food and drink, live music and caroling, photo spots, a Santa visit and a light-up dance floor. Ice skating, a snow slide and a s'mores pit cost extra, as does parking (free lots are first come, first served). You pick an arrival window when you book and can then stay until closing; the event is cashless and only soft bags up to 16x16x8 in are allowed.

hook: The Philharmonic's all-new Vegas-style holiday pops concert

Five singers from Strip shows join the orchestra for classics, carols and sing-alongs, with a children's choir and Nevada Ballet Theatre dancing the Waltz of the Flowers from The Nutcracker. Santa and the Grinch both drop in, and the orchestra promises more surprises. It plays in Reynolds Hall at The Smith Center downtown, a dressy-but-fun date night before or after dinner nearby.

hook: Balanchine's classic Nutcracker with a live orchestra downtown
description: Nevada Ballet Theatre brings back George Balanchine's version of The Nutcracker, which it first staged in 2025, with the Las Vegas Philharmonic playing Tchaikovsky's score live. The production mixes traditional sets and costumes with projected media, following Marie and her Nutcracker Prince from the Christmas Eve party and the battle with the Mouse King through the snow forest to the Land of Sweets. Expect the big set pieces: the snowflake waltz, Dewdrop, the Sugarplum Fairy, Mother Ginger and her Polichinelles. Act I runs 49 minutes, then a 20-minute intermission and a 41-minute Act II, at The Smith Center's Reynolds Hall.

hook: The NYC comedy landmark's Vegas club: five headliners a night
description: The first West Coast branch of New York's famous Comedy Cellar, the club that helped launch Ray Romano, Jon Stewart and Amy Schumer, sits in an intimate 300-seat underground room at the Rio. It uses the same showcase format as the original: five headliner-level comics each do a 15-20 minute set, so you get a real mix in one show. Lineups change weekly and are posted on the Rio page (Thanksgiving week includes Tom Rhodes and Butch Bradley with host Mark Cohen). There are two shows every night, and the club now serves shareable bites and cocktails. Guests must be 18 or older.
address: Rio Hotel & Casino, 3700 W Flamingo Rd, Las Vegas, NV 89103

name: Herbs & Rye
price_note: Prices not posted.
hours_note: 5 pm to 3 am Monday to Saturday; Sunday not listed on the site. Holiday hours not posted.
description: An off-Strip cocktail bar and steakhouse on West Sahara, open since 2009. The house line is that they make 'pretty good steaks, and REALLY good cocktails'. It stays open until 3 am six nights a week, so it works as a late dinner or a nightcap away from the casinos. Book ahead for a table.
hook: Serious cocktails and steaks off-Strip, open till 3 am
address: 3713 W Sahara Ave, Las Vegas, NV 89102

name: Esther's Kitchen
price_note: Moderate ($$). Parties of 6+ get a $15 per person credit-card hold.
hours_note: Lunch 11 am-3 pm weekdays, brunch 10 am-3 pm weekends, dinner 5-11 pm daily. Holiday hours not posted.
description: Chef James Trees' seasonal Italian restaurant in the Arts District, named for the great-aunt who got him cooking. The menu leans on West Coast produce and Italian tradition, and it has been praised by Food & Wine and USA Today 10Best. The dining room is warm and moody, with an open kitchen, leather booths and big hanging lamps. It does weekend brunch as well as lunch and dinner; there is street and lot parking nearby.
hook: Chef-run seasonal Italian in the Arts District
address: 1131 S Main St, Las Vegas, NV 89104

name: Carson Kitchen
price_note: Happy hour Mon-Fri 3-5 pm at the bar: grilled oysters $3 each, deviled eggs $3, gyro tacos $5, tempura green beans $6, select beers $5, wine $8, well drinks $6.
hours_note: 11:30 am-10 pm Sunday to Thursday, until 11 pm Friday and Saturday. Holiday hours not posted.
description: A downtown favourite since 2014 inside the John E. Carson Hotel, a repurposed mid-century motel at Carson Ave and 6th St. The food is reimagined comfort food made with fine-dining ingredients, plus crafted cocktails. There is a bar, an open kitchen counter, community tables, a courtyard and an outdoor rooftop bar. Weekday happy hour (3-5 pm, bar only) has $3 grilled oysters and $6 well drinks.
hook: Shareable comfort food and a rooftop bar downtown
highlights: Opened 2014 by Cory Harwell and the late Kerry Simon
address: 124 S 6th St, Suite 100, Las Vegas, NV 89101

name: Double Down Saloon
price_note: Free entry: all shows are free. Drink prices not posted.
hours_note: The bar says 'We Never Close'. Band and DJ nights usually start 9-10 pm; a punk rock matinee is listed Dec 5, 2-6 pm.
description: A self-described punk rock dive off Paradise Road, open around the clock, with walls covered in wild murals, pool, pinball and video poker. Live bands and DJ nights are free, and the bar's motto is 'Shut up & drink!'. It celebrates its 34th anniversary Nov 25-28 with nightly shows, and December brings punk nights, a Saturday punk rock matinee and a New Year's Eve video jukebox. Smoking is allowed, so it is a rowdy late-night stop rather than a quiet date.
hook: 24-hour punk dive with free shows
age_note: Bar, 21+ presumed; age rule not posted
address: 4640 Paradise Rd, Las Vegas, NV 89169

name: minus5 Ice Bar (The Venetian)
price_note: Cool package $26 (entry, gloves, parka); Coolest $49 (adds 2 ice cocktails); V-ICE-P $79 (faux-fur coat, 2 cocktails, digital photo, hat). Kids 7-12: $19 or $29.
hours_note: Daily 11 am-11 pm. Kids 7-12 welcome before 9 pm with an adult. Holiday hours not posted.
description: A bar where the walls, seats, sculptures and even the glasses are carved from ice, kept frozen. You get gloves and a parka (or a faux-fur coat on the top package) at the door, then wander the glowing ice rooms and take photos with a cocktail served in an ice glass. Packages run from entry only ($26) to two cocktails, a digital photo and a hat ($79). It is on Level 2 of the Grand Canal Shoppes, at the end of the canal, across from Skechers.
hook: Drinks in glasses made of ice, below freezing
highlights: Everything made of ice, glasses too
age_note: Ages 7-12 welcome before 9 pm with an adult; cocktails 21+
address: The Grand Canal Shoppes, 3377 S Las Vegas Blvd, Suite 2140, Las Vegas, NV 89109

name: Evel Pie
price_note: Prices not posted.
hours_note: 11 am-2 am Sunday to Thursday, 11 am-4 am Friday and Saturday. Closed Thanksgiving and Christmas Day; Christmas Eve 11 am-8 pm; New Year's Eve 11 am-3 am.
description: A rowdy pizza joint on Fremont East with the motto 'Live Hard - Ride Fast - Eat Pizza'. It serves pizza and draft beer and stays open until 2 am (4 am at weekends), so it is an easy late-night stop downtown. The site also lists live music and a 'reaper' eating contest. Walk in; there is a gift-shop line of joint gear too.
hook: Late-night pizza joint on Fremont East, open till 4 am weekends
highlights: Live music and a reaper contest
age_note: Restaurant and bar; age rules not posted
address: 508 Fremont St, Las Vegas, NV 89101

name: Top of Binion's Steakhouse
price_note: Prices are on the restaurant's menu.
hours_note: 5-10 pm Thursday to Monday; closed Tuesday and Wednesday. Holiday hours not posted.
description: A vintage steakhouse on the 24th floor of Binion's, first opened as 'Top of The Mint' when the Mint tower was finished in 1965. The draw is the view plus an old-Vegas, romantic room. Steaks are 40-day-aged Certified Angus Beef cut in-house and charbroiled; menu examples include rib eye, prime rib, cowboy steak, chicken-fried lobster, lobster Newburg and a vegetarian mushroom risotto. Dinner only, five nights a week; reserve on OpenTable or by phone.
hook: 24th-floor steakhouse with downtown views, since 1965
highlights: Opened 1965 as Top of The Mint
address: Binion's Gambling Hall, 128 E Fremont St, Las Vegas, NV 89101

name: Oscar's Steakhouse (Plaza glass dome)
price_note: Happy hour daily 5-7 pm in the bar and lounge (not holidays): house wine $7, well cocktails $6, domestic beer $3, imported beer $4.
hours_note: Daily 5-10 pm; happy hour 5-7 pm in the lounge (not on holidays). Business or upscale casual dress.
description: A steakhouse named for Oscar Goodman, the former mob lawyer turned Las Vegas mayor, with its main dining room inside the Plaza's iconic glass dome. It plays up old Vegas with memorabilia, handcrafted cocktails (including the mayor's own martini), steaks, classic seafood and family-recipe sides. There is a big lounge and a rooftop patio, and daily happy hour has $6 well cocktails and 'No Nose's meatballs'. Dress code is business or upscale casual: no gym wear, tank tops or flip-flops.
hook: Steak under the Plaza's glass dome, named for the mob-lawyer mayor
highlights: Dining room in the Plaza's glass dome
address: Plaza Hotel & Casino, 1 Main St, Las Vegas, NV 89101

name: Able Baker Brewing (Arts District taproom)
price_note: Small fee for street and lot parking.
hours_note: 11:30 am-11 pm Sunday to Thursday, until 1 am Friday and Saturday. Holiday hours not posted.
description: An Arts District brewery and taproom whose beers and decor nod to Nevada's Atomic Age and state history. There are more than 30 craft beers on tap, a scratch kitchen, long wooden communal tables and the brewhouse tanks in view. No reservations, just walk in; brewery tours and private events can be booked through the site. All ages are welcome in the taproom, but under-21s cannot sit at or approach the bar.
hook: Atomic Age-themed brewery with 30+ taps in the Arts District
age_note: All ages in the taproom; under 21 not allowed at the bar
address: 1510 S Main St, Suite 120, Las Vegas, NV 89104

name: Shang Artisan Noodle
price_note: Fast-casual and affordable.
hours_note: Daily 11 am-10 pm. Holiday hours not posted.
description: A fast-casual noodle shop west of the Strip that makes Shan-Xi style noodles by hand, kneading and pulling the dough in the traditional northern Chinese way. The noodles are silky and springy and go into both hot and cold dishes. It is cheap, quick and open every day until 10 pm, a good off-Strip lunch or casual dinner near Chinatown.
hook: Hand-pulled Shan-Xi noodles, off-Strip and affordable
address: 4983 W Flamingo Rd, Suite B, Las Vegas, NV 89103

name: Dig This (heavy equipment playground)
price_note: Big Dig Excavators and Big Dig Bulldozer from $359 (90 min); Aggression Session from $799 (45 min); custom digs for 4+ people priced on request.
hours_note: Opening hours not posted; book a time slot online or call. Holiday hours not posted.
description: Dig This lets you climb into real construction machines, such as a full-size excavator or bulldozer, and play in a giant dirt yard just off the Strip. Each session starts with a safety briefing and in-cab training on every lever and button, then an instructor coaches you by radio while you dig trenches, move mounds and try challenges. No experience or driver's license is needed, and the cabs are heated and air-conditioned, so winter weather is not a problem. Most sessions are for 1-4 operators; groups of 4 or more can build a custom dig, and there are separate kids digs.
hook: Drive a real bulldozer or excavator in a giant Vegas sandbox
highlights: Big Dig Excavators: from $359, 90 min, ages 12+
Big Dig Bulldozer: from $359, 90 min, ages 14+
No driver's license needed; climate-controlled cabs
Reschedule or credit with 72+ hours' notice
age_note: Ages 12+ for excavators, 14+ for bulldozer and Aggression Session; separate kids digs exist.
address: 800 W Roban Ave, Las Vegas, NV 89044

name: Zak Bagans' The Haunted Museum
price_note: General admission from $54. Discounts for Nevada residents, seniors 65+ and active/retired military (ID required). RIP All Access ticket and Late Night Flashlight Ghost Tour cost extra.
hours_note: Wednesday-Monday 1-9 pm; closed Tuesdays. Holiday hours not posted.
description: Ghost Adventures host Zak Bagans fills the historic Wengert Mansion near downtown with his collection of supposedly haunted and macabre objects: rooms of oddities, puppets, a funeral room and infamous artifacts. Visits are guided tours of about two hours that leave roughly every 10-15 minutes within your reserved time block. Reservations are strongly advised because slots sell out; walk-ups are limited. Ghost-hunting gear is not allowed on regular tours, but the Late Night Flashlight Ghost Tour lets 30 guests roam the whole museum for 90 minutes with recorders and EMF meters.
hook: A celebrity ghost hunter's haunted mansion museum
highlights: From $54; resident, senior and military discounts
Late Night Flashlight Ghost Tour: 30 guests, 90 min
RIP All Access ticket adds extra exhibits, badge and T-shirt
Gift shop open without a tour
address: 600 E Charleston Blvd, Las Vegas, NV 89104

photos.credit: Zak Bagans' The Haunted Museum (official site)

name: Burlesque Hall of Fame museum
price_note: Admission price not posted.
hours_note: Hours not posted; call (888) 661-6465 before going.
description: A small museum in the Arts District run by the nonprofit Burlesque Hall of Fame, which preserves the history of burlesque. It holds costumes, photos and memorabilia from legends such as Gypsy Rose Lee, Lili St. Cyr, Tempest Storm, Sally Rand and Jennie Lee, and has a museum store. It pairs well with an evening of Arts District bars and galleries on Main Street.
hook: Feathers, fans and showgirl history in the Arts District
highlights: Memorabilia of Gypsy Rose Lee, Lili St. Cyr, Tempest Storm
On S Main St in the Arts District
address: 1027 S Main St #110, Las Vegas, NV 89101

name: Silverton Aquarium & Mermaid Swims
price_note: Free to watch. Dive Ventures for certified divers: $300, select weekends, advance inquiry required.
hours_note: Aquarium viewable 24/7. Mermaids swim Thursday-Saturday noon-8 pm and Sunday 10:30 am-6:30 pm, every half hour, with a break 3:45-5 pm. Stingray feedings daily at 1:30 and 4:30 pm.
description: Inside the lodge-themed Silverton casino, a 117,000-gallon reef tank holds thousands of tropical fish, rays and sharks, and it can be watched for free at any hour. Thursday to Sunday, live mermaids swim through the tank every half hour, and daily interactive stingray feedings happen at 1:30 and 4:30 pm. Certified divers can book a 30-40 minute dive in the tank on select weekends. It is an easy, free stop on the south end of town.
hook: Free 117,000-gallon aquarium with live mermaids
highlights: Mermaids Thu-Sat noon-8 pm, Sun 10:30 am-6:30 pm
Certified divers: $300 tank dive, select weekends
age_note: Inside a casino; the aquarium page lists no age rule.
address: 3333 Blue Diamond Rd, Las Vegas, NV 89139

name: Goldwell Open Air Museum (near Rhyolite ghost town)
neighborhood: Beatty, NV (day trip, on the road to Death Valley)
price_note: Admission price not posted.
hours_note: Sculpture park open 24 hours, every day. Visitor center and gift shop roughly Monday-Saturday 10 am-4 pm.
description: In the open Mojave desert just outside the Rhyolite ghost town, on the road toward Death Valley, a group of Belgian artists led by Albert Szukalski placed seven large outdoor sculptures, including ghostly plaster-shrouded figures. You walk among the works freely at any hour, then can wander the ruins of Rhyolite next door. The park is private property; personal photography is welcome. It won Best Sculpture Park in the 2026 USA Today 10Best Readers' Choice awards, and makes a striking stop on a Death Valley road trip.
hook: Ghostly desert sculptures next to a real ghost town
highlights: Visitor center Mon-Sat about 10 am-4 pm
Next to Rhyolite ghost town, on the way to Death Valley
address: 1 Golden St, Beatty, NV 89003

name: Sky Combat Ace (stunt-plane and dogfight flights)
price_note: Operation Recon ride-along $599; The Afterburner (you fly the aerobatics) $999; Air-to-Air Dogfighting from $1,299; Top Gun Experience from $1,999; all per person.
hours_note: Flights 7 am-5 pm Sunday, Monday and Thursday-Saturday; Tuesday and Wednesday not listed. Booked by time slot; holiday hours not posted.
description: Sky Combat Ace flies guests in real aerobatic stunt planes from North Las Vegas Airport. The cheapest option is a ride-along where a stunt pilot throws the plane through rolls, dives and zero-G moments; higher tiers let you take the stick for loops and rolls with an instructor beside you, or fly simulated air-to-air dogfights against a friend or partner. The top package is a multi-plane, Top Gun-style combat mission. Plan about 3 hours in total for most packages (4 for Top Gun), including briefing.
hook: Fly loops or dogfight your partner in a real stunt plane
highlights: Ride-along stunt flight: $599, about 3 hours total
Top Gun multi-ship mission from $1,999, about 4 hours
age_note: Check age, weight and health rules before booking.
address: 2634 Airport Dr #106, North Las Vegas, NV 89032

name: Round1 Bowling & Arcade (Meadows Mall)
price_note: Bowling, billiards and karaoke prices are on the venue's price page.
hours_note: Daily 10 am-2 am. Holiday hours not posted.
description: Round1's Las Vegas store at Meadows Mall puts an arcade, bowling lanes, a VIP immersive bowling lane, billiards, private karaoke rooms and a Victory Zone under one roof. It is open until 2 am every day, which makes it an easy late-night plan with friends off the Strip. Party rooms can be booked for groups. Round1 also lists a second store at the Las Vegas Outlets.
hook: Japanese mega-arcade with bowling and karaoke, open till 2 am
age_note: Check age rules with the venue.
address: 4300 Meadows Ln, Las Vegas, NV 89107
